title: Moussaka
method: Salt eggplant slices and let them rest 20 minutes, then pat dry.
Brush with olive oil and roast until lightly browned.
In a pan, sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add ground lamb and cook until browned.
Stir in tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, wine, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; simmer 20 minutes.
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish.
Pour béchamel over the top and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 40 minutes until golden.

title: Souvlaki
method: Mix olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Marinate meat cubes in the mixture for at least 1 hour.
Thread the meat onto skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat for 10–12 minutes, turning occasionally.
Serve hot with pita bread and tzatziki.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
method: Combine tomatoes, cucumber, onion, and olives in a bowl.
Place a block of feta on top.
Drizzle olive oil over the salad.
Sprinkle oregano and salt.
Toss lightly before serving.

title: Spanakopita
method: Sauté onion until soft, then add spinach and cook until wilted.
Mix spinach mixture with eggs, feta, dill, salt, and pepper.
Layer phyllo sheets in an oiled baking dish.
Spread the spinach filling evenly.
Cover with remaining phyllo sheets, brushing with oil.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 35–40 minutes until golden.

title: Dolmades
method: Sauté onion in olive oil until soft.
Add rice, dill, salt, and pepper and cook briefly.
Place a spoonful of filling on each grape leaf and roll tightly.
Arrange rolls in a pot and cover with water and lemon juice.
Simmer for 35 minutes until rice is tender.

title: Tzatziki
method: Drain grated cucumber to remove excess liquid.
Mix yogurt, cucumber, garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, dill, and salt.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.

title: Pastitsio
method: Cook pasta until al dente.
Brown ground beef with onion.
Add tomato sauce, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; simmer 15 minutes.
Layer pasta, meat sauce, and béchamel in a baking dish.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 40 minutes.

title: Baklava
method: Layer buttered phyllo sheets in a baking dish.
Sprinkle walnuts and cinnamon between layers.
Top with remaining phyllo and butter.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 40 minutes.
Simmer sugar, honey, and water into syrup.
Pour syrup over hot baklava.

title: Loukoumades
method: Mix flour, yeast, and water into a smooth batter.
Let it rise until doubled.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry until golden.
Drizzle with honey and sprinkle with cinnamon.

title: Fasolada
method: Soak beans overnight and cook until tender.
Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in olive oil.
Add cooked beans and tomato sauce.
Simmer for 40 minutes until flavors meld.
Season and serve.

title: Gyros
method: Season meat with olive oil, oregano, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Cook in a hot pan or grill until browned.
Warm pita bread.
Fill pita with meat, tomato, onion, and tzatziki.
Wrap and serve.

title: Kleftiko
method: Season lamb with olive oil, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Place lamb, potatoes, and lemon in a baking dish.
Cover tightly with foil.
Bake at 325°F (160°C) for 2 hours until tender.

title: Saganaki
method: Coat cheese lightly in flour.
Heat olive oil in a skillet.
Fry cheese until golden on both sides.
Serve immediately with lemon.

title: Avgolemono Soup
method: Bring broth to a boil and cook rice until tender.
Whisk eggs and lemon juice together.
Slowly add hot broth to egg mixture while whisking.
Return mixture to soup and heat gently without boiling.
Season and serve.

title: Galaktoboureko
method: Heat milk with semolina and sugar to make a thick custard.
Stir in eggs and vanilla once slightly cooled.
Layer buttered phyllo in a baking dish and add custard.
Cover with remaining phyllo.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 40 minutes.
Simmer sugar, water, and lemon peel into syrup.
Pour syrup over hot pastry.
